WEATHER ADVISORY — Harlow County Emergency Services
Issued: Friday, April 3, 6:00 A.M.
A severe storm system is expected to move through Harlow County between Saturday morning and Sunday afternoon. Forecasters predict sustained winds of up to 70 kilometers per hour, heavy rainfall, and possible localized flooding in low-lying areas, particularly near the Brennan River. Residents are advised to secure outdoor furniture, avoid unnecessary travel on Saturday, and keep mobile devices charged. Organizers of outdoor gatherings of more than 50 people are strongly urged to postpone events scheduled for this weekend. Updates will be posted at www.harlowcounty.gov/alerts every three hours.

--- Passage 2 ---
To: Registered Participants
From: Dana Whitfield, Riverside Run Committee
Subject: Postponement of the 10K Riverside Run
Date: Friday, April 3

Dear Runners,
In light of the advisory issued by Harlow County Emergency Services this morning, the committee has decided to postpone the 10K Riverside Run originally scheduled for Saturday, April 4. Because our course runs directly alongside the Brennan River, the flooding risk mentioned in the advisory makes it unsafe to proceed. The race has been rescheduled for Saturday, April 18, starting at the same location and time, 8:00 A.M. at Pelham Gate. Your registration and bib number will carry over automatically. Runners who cannot attend the new date may request a full refund by April 10 through our website. We apologize for the inconvenience and thank you for your understanding.
Dana Whitfield

Crestline Living Magazine — Reader Survey Results (Spring Issue)
Last quarter, 2,150 subscribers completed our annual readership survey. Key findings:
• 64% of respondents said they read the magazine primarily for home renovation features.
• 58% wanted more short, practical articles of under two pages.
• Only 19% reported reading the monthly celebrity interview, the lowest score of any regular section.
• 47% said they would pay extra for a digital archive of past issues.
• The gardening column received the highest satisfaction rating for the third consecutive year.
Respondents aged 25-40 made up 51 percent of participants, a notable increase from 38 percent two years ago.

--- Passage 2 ---
MEMO
To: Editorial Staff
From: Priya Raman, Editor in Chief
Date: June 1
Re: Content changes for the autumn issue

Having reviewed the survey results published in our spring issue, I am making the following changes beginning with the autumn issue. First, the celebrity interview will be discontinued; its page count will be reassigned to a new series of two-page renovation guides, which aligns with what most readers told us they want. Second, given the satisfaction ratings, Hannah Cho's column will be expanded from one page to two. Finally, the digital team will present a proposal for a paid online archive at the July planning meeting. Please send any concerns to me by June 12.
Priya
